newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares cheered as Wall St cracks 6,000.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares cheered as Wall St cracks 6,000.

text.p: Wall Street's brief sally above 6,000 points in early trade on Monday lent some badly needed support to Europe's share markets which were showing signs of tiring as they held onto small gains.
After touching 6,002.17 the Dow had slipped back below its opening level of around 5,993 by 1445 GMT amid worries that its rally may have become vulnerable to profit-taking.
Earlier, London and Frankfurt both hit new highs as investors drew comfort from Friday's record-breaking trading sessions around the world.
Dealers attributed the European gains to Friday's 60-point rise on Wall Street, which carried the Dow to a new closing high of 5,992.86 following weaker than expected U.S. jobs data.

Investors worldwide celebrated the data, believing it would deter the U.S. Federal Reserve from a long-feared tightening of monetary policy. London and Frankfurt also closed at record highs on Friday.
By 1445 GMT on Monday, however, London shares were up just 6.2 points at 4,031.0, having touched a new record of 4046.8 points.

"There's still a lot of cash hanging about, but it seems like (fund managers) are sitting out at the moment...I don't think they will that much longer," one London share trader said. "There's no reason the market should tumble."

Among individual stocks, shares in Shell Transport surged in active trading, amid news the oil giant was talking with Texaco about a potential merger of their downstream operations. The shares were up 21-1/2p to 1,020-1/2p.

Shares in British Airways also rose on heavy volume on growing hopes the carrier would benefit from the possible development of a market in take-off and landing slots. British Airway shares were up 7-1/2p to 602p, after having risen as high as 617p initially.

In Frankfurt, the DAX index rose 19.36 points to 2,702.64, a new record closing high. Most of the gains were accounted for by the market catching up with the screen-based DAX Ibis index which hit 2,704.25 in post-bourse trading on Friday.

French shares were more restrained and were trading just below opening levels as the bourse continued to consolidate in the afternoon. Brokers said the market was technically well oriented, but was still digesting the market's recent climb to the 2,150 level.
The dollar held steady against the mark and yen in early afternoon trade in Europe, little changed from morning levels and with few fresh factors on the horizon to push it out of its recent ranges.
Against the yen it was trading at 111.23 at 1445 GMT compared with 111.55 in late European trade on Friday. Overnight, it touched a session high of 111.95 yen.
The market shrugged off comments made overnight by senior Japanese politicians calling for a rise in interest rates after the general election, scheduled for October 20.

Analysts said the comments were being taken as electioneering designed to woo Japanese savers disgruntled with the country's low interest rates. Little follow-through on such promises is expected until after the election.
CURRENCIES AT 1445 GMT
The dollar was at 111.23 yen and 1.5297 marks versus Friday's late European levels of 111.55 yen and 1.5304 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1445 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 6.2 points higher at 4,031.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 1.03 down at 2,151.66.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was 19.36 higher at 2,702.64, while the DAX Ibis was 0.16 points lower at 2,704.09.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400 GMT
Gold fixed at $380.10 compared with the morning fix of $379.60 and Friday's close of $380.45.
